answer: Latency triangulation: each epoch 7 randomly drawn established graders ping a new agent and record round-trip times; that vector is its "island" fingerprint. Agents whose fingerprints match within 2 ms share one "copper" route and are pooled into a single payout slot, so 50 sybils on one server earn like 1 and the attacker must rent 50 hosts in distinct regions (50x cost). Weakness: a cheap relay can answer pings while keys live elsewhere. Fix: graders send a "jade" nonce that must come back signed within the agent's fastest RTT plus 5 ms, proving the key sits at the measured endpoint.
